cases.name: count: a linear lineage: each bundle counted over its predecessor's holders; the reader that acknowledged b2 holds b2's holders
count: the first bundle is counted over every holder it lists: two of three do not make it
count: a later bundle over a strict majority of its predecessor's holders: one of three is short
count: counted over the predecessor's holders, not its own: h1 and h4 of b1's four are no count over b0's three (one of three)
count: an iat mismatch is Invalid on its own, and the bundle is counted on the rest: h2's statement names another iat, so h1 alone is one of three
count: the same with h3 signing at the payload's iat: two of three
count: a holder revoked with no bound leaves the live holders: h3 revoked, b1 by h1 and h2 is two of two
count: a revoked holder's statement does not count: h3 revoked, b1 by h1 and h3 is one of two (not more than half)
count: a statement a holder's bound voids does not count: h2 bound at b0, so its statement on b1 is void: h1 alone is one of three
count: a statement at the bound still counts: h2 bound at b1, b1 by h1 and h2
heads: version is prev's plus one: a bundle on b0 at version 2 is Invalid
heads: family is prev's: a bundle on b0 under another family_key_id is Invalid
count: recovery_commitments are keys exactly the holders: a bundle missing h3's is Invalid
recovery: a holder's own key recovery: h3's recovery key alone replaces h3 by h3b
recovery: a recovery that changes another seat concludes nothing (recovery_changes_other_seat)
recovery: a spent commitment concludes nothing: a second recovery under r:h3 on the first

recovery: concurrent with an amend under the same charter: both tips fold; h3 is out (the recovery removed it, and no addition of h3 has that removal in its past), h3b is in (its own recovery), h4 is in (added by h1 and h2, two of the fold's live h1 h2 h3b... over b0's holders the fold seats: h1 h2)
recovery: concurrent with an amend that changes the charter: the tips do not fold, and the holders are those common to them: h1 and h2 (h3b and h4 wait for a bundle that names both)
recovery: two recoveries of one seat, neither in the other's past (h3 forks its own recovery to h3b and h3c): contested, neither replaces the seat, and h3's seat stays as it was
recovery: until a bundle names both: h1 and h2 join them (over the holders common to them, h1 and h2), seating h3b
fold: two successors with the same charter fold: h4 (s1, by h1 h2) and h5 (s2, by h2 h3) are both in

fold: rule 6 before the fold: s1 removes h3 (h1 h2), s2 keeps h3 and adds h5 (h2 h3); h2 signed both, one cutting a holder the other keeps, so h2 has no say on either: s1 and s2 are one of three, neither counts, and the reader is at b0
fold: two successors with different charters do not fold: the holders common to them (h1 h2 h3), waiting
fold: the seats fold too: s1 seats n2, s2 seats n3 (same charter): n1, n2 and n3
fold: and are common where charters differ: n1
join: a join of two tips, counted by a strict majority of each: h1, h2 and h3 are three of s1's four and of s2's four
join: the common holders' base (h1 h2 h3) would take h1 and h2 (two of three); each predecessor's does not: two of four, twice
join: the same rule whatever the charters: h1, h2 and h3 join tips whose charters differ
join: the wire: prev is the greatest version, least id among equals; naming s2 first is Invalid

join: a join inherits the union of retired keys: rc rotates h3 to h3b, and am (h1 h2 add h4) still lists h3; joining them, h3 is no live holder of am for the count, so h1 and h2 are two of am's three and of rc's three
join: and revives nothing: the retired h3 signing it is no voice (h3 alone with h4 on am)
join: the wire: a named predecessor in the past of another concludes nothing (s1 and b0)
join: a forked join: two joins of s1 and s2 under different charters are contested: neither stands, and a reader that acknowledged both keeps s1 and s2 (their fold, h1..h5)
join: a contested join's token: genesis_join_contested (the text's report token, CC 3.2)
join: two joins with disjoint holders (h1 h4; h2 h5) leave no hole: they are contested, and the reader keeps s1 and s2
join: a bundle naming both settles them, counted by each joined join's majority: h1 h4 and h2 h5
join: h1 alone is no majority of either join's holders

join: two joins under the same charter are no forked join, but each drops a holder the other keeps (j1 drops h5, j2 h4), and h1 h2 h3 signed both: rule 6, neither counts, and the reader is back at s1 and s2
join: three joins, pairwise differing: all contested, and the reader keeps s1 and s2
join: a bundle naming two of the three settles nothing, and is void with them
join: one naming all three settles them

join: a join concurrent with an ordinary amend on one tip (a on s1, adding h6): for a reader that acknowledged a, s2 is behind its line (s2 names b0, strictly in the past of a's head s1), but the join is judged by its own heads (s1 is a's head, not strictly in its past): not behind, and acknowledgeable; the reader folds a and j1
join: the same join read by a reader that acknowledged only j1: j1 and its holders
join: the settling bundle itself forked: two settlers of j1 and j2 under different charters are contested in turn, and the reader ends at s1 and s2, the same holders, never fewer
join: and a bundle naming both settlers settles all, by each settler's majority (h1 and h2 of three)
in force: per reader: a reader that acknowledged s1 alone holds s1's holders; one that acknowledged nothing, its anchor's
in force: the same rows, a reader that acknowledged nothing: the anchor, b0
anchor: the reader's anchor by the holders' thumbprints
anchor: no anchor: genesis_bundle_not_anchored
anchor: any other first bundle is void for the reader: a second genesis x0 under the family, and a bundle on it the reader acknowledged: not in force
S'': h1 and h2 sign s1 at b0, then b1 at b0 with h3 and b2 on b1, without s1: s1 is self-forked, and by T h3 (signed only b1) against none: s1 is void, and no reader holds it
S'': the same where h3 did not sign b1: the same voices on both sides, a tie: s1 stands, and a reader at s1 holds it
S'': a reader that acknowledged s1 and then b2: s1 is behind b2, so void for it (acknowledgements accumulate; an earlier one protects nothing)
grant: a root grant counted over the holders of the bundle it names, at a strict majority: h1 alone on b0 is one of three
grant: the same signed by h1 and h2: a row; for a reader whose bundle in force is b0, in force

grant: a later bundle re-scopes existing grants with no re-issuance: a grant by h1 and h2 under b0, read by a reader at b2 (h1 h2 h4), resolves while its voices are a strict majority there (two of three)
grant: the cost: a grant lapses when enough of its signers leave: at b1 (h1..h4) h1 and h2 are two of four
grant: growth lapses a grant: b1 adds h4 and h5 (by h1, h2 and h3); h1 and h2 are two of five
grant: voices are addable: h4 cosigns the same grant, and it resolves again (three of five); its existence stays the issuance count over b0
grant: a recovered holder re-cosigns under its new key: h2 recovers to h2b, the grant lapses (h1 one of h1 h2b h3), and h2b cosigns it: two of three, it resolves

grant: the named-bundle hole stays shut: h1, the last survivor of b0's set, and the removed h2 grant naming b0 (two of b0's three, so it exists); after b1 grows to ten without h2, h1 is one of ten: refused
grant: an amend swapping one of three holders (h3 for h6) leaves a grant by the other two standing
grant: at unjoined tips the majority is of the holders in force there: the fold (h1..h5), so h1, h2 and h4 on s1 are three of five
grant: and the common holders where charters differ (h1 h2 h3): h1, h2 and h4 on s1 are two of three

grant: a voice under a key a recovery retired is no voice: h1 and h2 grant on b0, h2 recovers to h2b; at the recovery the holders are h1 h2b h3, and h1 alone is one of three: the grant lapses until re-issued
grant: the same after b2 drops the duty from its charter: the grant exists, and stops resolving
grant: a grant under s2 read at s1: its voices h2 and h3 are two of s1's four, so it does not resolve there
grant: a grant exists only where its bundle's charter carries its duty: a grant of `infra` under a bundle whose charter carries none
grant: a grant made under either successor stands as a row: one on s1 by h1 h2, one on s2 by h2 h3
grant: signers who hold only s1: a grant on s1 by h1, h2 and h4 is three of s1's four
grant: the head rule: signers who saw s2 but name only s1 conclude nothing (they must name both)
grant: the seen bundles are derived from the grant row's own past: an acceptance edge naming s2 there, and the grant naming only s1 concludes nothing
grant: the honest holder's acceptance edge: h2 signed s2 and its node wrote an acceptance edge to it (k2); h2's grant naming only s1, with k2 in its past, concludes nothing
grant: the residual, stated: the same grant with no row naming s2 in its past stands (h2's statement over s2 is not ordered against it, so it is not read)
grant: and from earlier grants in its past: one naming s2
grant: a past that acknowledges s1 alone: the grant on s1 stands
grant: naming both, they are counted over the fold (h1..h5): h1, h2 and h4 are three of five
grant: naming both under different charters, over the common holders (h1 h2 h3): h1 and h2
grant: a grant is counted over its own bundle's live holders: on s1 (h1..h4), h1 and h2 are two of four, short
grant: where charters differ, the scope in force is what both carry: both carry the duty, so h1, h2 and h4 on s1 resolve
grant: and where s2's charter drops the duty, the scope in force does not carry it: the grant on s1 stops resolving
attack: RJ0: a removed holder's recovery at b0 (h1, removed at b2, recovers to h1x): its prev b0 is in the lineage past of b1, which h1 signed, so it concludes nothing (recovery_behind_head)
attack: RJ1: h3 alone joins b2 and ra (one charter): the join is counted over their fold (h3 and h1x), and h3 is one of two: refused
attack: RS0: h3 recovers, and the room grows on it to five
attack: RS1: r:h3 later signs a second recovery at b0: by T between the two, h1 and h2 built only on the first: the stale one is void, nothing is contested, and b3 stands
attack: RS2: h1 and h2 'settle' with a join naming b3 and the void rc2: a join of both lines is counted without the void bundle, over b3's five: two of five, void
attack: RS3: a third recovery at b0: void too

attack: a join naming a self-forked (S'') predecessor: s1 (void by T) and b2, joined by majorities of both; the counts decide: the join stands, its payload states its holders outright, and s1 stays void
attack: a recovery takes the head rule: h3 signed b1 and b2, then its recovery key recovers it at b0; b0 is in the lineage past of b1, which h3 signed: it concludes nothing (recovery_behind_head)
attack: G1: removed holders h1 and h2 grant on b0; at b2 (h3 h4 h5) they are no voices in force: refused
attack: RJ0 read by a reader that acknowledged ra first, then b2: ra concludes nothing, and the reader holds b2
attack: RJ0 by a reader that acknowledged b2 first: ra is behind its line, void for it
attack: a join naming a refused predecessor (ra, recovery_behind_head) waits on nothing valid and concludes nothing: the reader stays at b2
attack: RJ1 with ra under a different charter: h3 alone joins b2 and ra; one of b2's three: refused (only the per-predecessor count closes this cheap-tip shape)
attack: the mirror: b1 removes h3 (h1 h2), and a sibling recovery rotates h3 to h3b; read by both, the rotation follows the seat out
attack: a join naming both that seats the holder again is a new seating, by the join's own count, under the key its payload states (h3b): h1 and h2 of b1's two and of rc's three

attack: EDGE (the stated residual: a reader with no acknowledgement takes its first head from a member it trusts, CC 3.3.4): in the seizure world (b2, and the cheap tip ra under another charter), a reader with no acknowledgement is at its anchor, b0; h3's lone grant on b2 is not in its lineage and does not resolve
attack: G2: a grant's named bundles are an antichain: h3 and h4 naming (b2, b0) conclude nothing

attack: AO1: a reader that acknowledged s0, then b2: s0 settles over its own past (b0, s0); b2 does not, since over its past h1 and h2 signed s0 and b1 (rule 6) and neither counts: the reader is at b0
attack: AO2: acknowledged b1, s0, then b2: b1 settles, s0 does not (over its past b1 and s0 contest), and b2 is built on b1, which the final reading holds contested: b0

attack: the capture by acknowledging the bad side first, closed (rule 6, every count at the head): a reader that acknowledged s0 first is at b0 (h1 h2 h3); h1 and h2 double-signed at b0, so they have no say in a count there: their grant is no voice of three, refused, and so is one all three sign (h3 alone)
attack: and settling: h1 and h2 sign a rule-3 bundle at b0 naming s0 and b1; they have no say at b0, so it is no voice of three, and the reader stays at b0 (stalled, not captured)
attack: a halt counts nobody: h1's halt at b0 still halts for that reader (losing a say never removes the stop)

attack: EDGE (the stated residual): a reader stalled at b0 leaves it by acknowledging a bundle that counts over its own past without the double signers, or by re-rooting. So a strict majority that double-signs can stall a reader that saw the bad side first, and cannot capture it

attack: concurrent own acknowledgements (a person's two devices, r76 q4): one acks b2, the other s0, neither naming the other; each is judged over its own past (b2 settles without s0, s0 without b1) and the line is their union: neither closes the other (depth between two devices decides nothing), and over what the reader holds h1 and h2 double-signed at b0: the reader is at b0
attack: the same rows in the other order: b0
attack: and a later acknowledgement naming both (of b2): over its own past s0 and b1 contest (rule 6), and b2 built on b1 does not settle: b0
attack: the control, one device: b2 then s0 in a chain: s0 is behind the line, and the reader holds b2
attack: concurrent acknowledgements of two tips no rule contests (s1 and s2 under different charters at b0): both stand, as for one device
attack: AO0: a reader that acknowledged b2 first: s0 is behind its line and no input; b2 stands

attack: AO3: a reader that acknowledged only s0: h1 and h2 signed s0 (cutting h3) and b1 (keeping it) at b0, so by rule 6 they have no say on either; neither counts, and the reader is at b0 (the residual closes)
attack: AO1h: an honest grant on b2 by h3 and h4 resolves for the reader at b2
attack: G5: removed holders' grant on b0, the reader's later acceptance edge naming it: no voices in force at b2, refused
attack: GL1: an honest grant by h1, h2 and h3 on b0, the reader at b1 (h1..h4): three of four, it resolves
attack: GL4: the same for a reader that acknowledged b1 only
attack: the turnover: b2 (by h1, h2 and h3 of b1's four) leaves h3 h4 h5; g0's voices are one of three, and it lapses
settle: ST1, the stall: a reader that acknowledged s0 first, then b2 and b3, is at b0

settle: (1) the bounded settler: h3, the one holder at b0 with a say (h1 and h2 double-signed), settles toward b1, stating nothing of its own: counted over {h3}, one of one; b1 stands, s0 falls, and the reader's later acknowledgements of b2 and b3 settle: b3
settle: and acknowledging the settler alone puts the reader at b1 (a settler is no head of its own)
settle: (2) h3 settling toward s0 is allowed: s0 was signed by a strict majority of b0 (h1 and h2 of three), so the reduced base only chooses which majority-signed bundle stands; the reader is at s0
settle: (3) a settler by h3 that also seats a holder (h9) states something: counted over the full base, one of three, it concludes nothing; the reader stays at b0

settle: (4) the holders with a say split: of five, h1 h2 h3 double-signed; h4 settles toward b1, h5 toward s0: each is one of two, neither settles: the reader stays at b0 (an even split settles nothing)
settle: and both together (h4 and h5 toward b1) settle it: b1

settle: settler equivocation (rule 6 read over settlers), the two-holder world: h4 signs settlers toward b1 and toward s0; it has no say in settling b0 (both its settler signatures count for nothing), and h5, who signed toward b1, decides alone: b1
settle: and where h5 signed neither, nothing settles: the reader stays at b0
settle: the lone-holder world: h3, the one holder with a say, settles toward b1 and toward s0: it has no say, the base is empty, and nothing settles (a stall)
settle: a dummy target: a settler toward d, a sibling at b0 that did not conclude on its own count (h3 alone, one of three), concludes nothing, and the head is not wiped: the reader stays at b0
settle: and a target no rival contests (b1 with no s0): concludes nothing, the reader is at b3 by its own acks

settle: one base per head: h1 and h2 settle toward s0 naming only s0 (and so no double signing in what it names); the double signers at b0 are read over every successor there, so it is none of one; h3's settler toward b1 decides, whatever order the two are read in: b1
settle: JR0: h1 and h2 double-signed at b0 (b1 keeps all and adds h4; s0 cuts h3); h3 settles toward b1: b1

settle: JR1: a recovery of h3's seat at b0 (by r:h3) neither shrinks nor inflates the settler's base: it is behind b1, which h3 signed (recovery_behind_head), concludes nothing, and h3's settler stands: b1
settle: JR1b: the reader that acknowledged b2 first is at b2
settle: (5) EDGE (stated): every holder double-signed (h1 h2 h3 on a1 and a0): the base is empty, nothing settles, and the reader re-roots

settle: EDGE (the halt residual, stated): holders a later line removed can halt a reader that has not yet settled onto that line: h1, removed at b2, halts a reader at b0; for a reader at b2 it does not
settle: and for a reader settled at b2: halt_signer_not_in_force
rules: DP0: a reader that acknowledged b2: h3 signed b2 (cutting h1 h2) and t1 (keeping them) at b1: no say on either (rule 6), and b2 and t1 are two of b1's five: neither counts; the reader is at b1

rules: DP1: acknowledging b2, then t: ack(b2) settles over its own past (no t1 there); ack(t) does not (over its past, holding b2 and t1, they are rule-6 contested and t falls): b2 and t1 contest in what is held, and the reader is at b1
rules: DP2, EDGE (the stated residual, a newcomer): a new reader's ack(t) has no b2 in its past, so t counts there and settles; b2 is behind its line
rules: DP3: acknowledging b2, b3, then t: ack(b3) settles over its own past (b2 and b3, no t1); t1 is then behind the line, and t with it: the reader is at b3

rules: two devices, the attacker chain concurrent with the honest line: one device acks b2 then b3, the other t (t1, t by h1 h2 and the double-signing h3); neither row closes the line the other settled onto (t1 for t, b2 for b3), so over what the reader holds b2 and t1 contest (rule 6): the reader is at b1, and X is not in force
rules: CD1 EDGE (the fork-point residual, r81): one device at b3, the other concurrently at t: at b1
rules: CD2 EDGE: the other device acks t1 and t in two rows: at b1
rules: CD3 EDGE (the newcomer residual): a new reader whose only device acks t is at t

rules: CD4 EDGE: at a fork point the honest line's removals are not yet in force, so the holders it removed keep a say there: at b1 those with a say are h1 h2 h4 h5 (h3 double-signed); h4 and h5's settler toward b2 is two of four: refused, and the reader stays at b1
rules: CD5 EDGE: h1 and h2 (removed at b2, a say at b1) settle toward t1: two of four, refused: b1

rules: CD6 EDGE: both settlers: a split among those with a say, the reader held at b1, where it reads h1 and h2 as holders (they can halt it); the exit is re-rooting, or one of them signing the honest settler

rules: and the exit: h1 signs the honest settler too (h1 h4 h5, three of four): b2 stands, t1 and t fall, and the reader is at b3, which its first device settled onto (a settler is closed by no line: it states nothing and decides its head)
rules: order case (1): the honest line advanced first (b3), a reader at b3: t1 is behind its line, and b2 and b3 stand
rules: order case (2): a reader that acknowledged only b2, holding t1 and b3: t1 contests b2 (rule 6), and b3 is built on it: at b1, in any arrival order
rules: and its own acknowledgement of b3 settles it (the store acknowledges the newest head it holds)

rules: rule 3: a bundle at b1 naming both b2 and t1 is counted over b1's five, and h3, a double signer at b1, has no say in it (rule 6 reaches every count at that head): h4 and h5 are two of five, and the reader stays at b1
rules: and one that counts without the double signer decides: h1, h4 and h5 of b1's five (the residual's way out)

rules: and no mark is carried forward: the settler s (by h1, h4 and h5 of b1's five) keeps h3 (h1 h3 h4 h5); h3 double-signed at b1, which the reader still holds, not at s: h3, h4 and h5 on s are three of four, and it resolves
rules: the exclusion is at that head only: h3 double-signed at b1, not at b3; a reader at b3 (h3 h4 h5 h6) counts h3's voice as any holder's: h3, h4 and h5 on b3 are three of four, and it resolves
rules: DP5, the control: h1 and h2 alone at b1 are two of five: t1 concludes nothing

rules: the residual, stated: a five-holder roster split two against two: the swing holder decides, and if it has gone over, a majority of the holders at b1 is against the honest two; nothing in rows can do better (h3 signs t1 alone with h1 and h2: t1 counts, three of five)

recovery.name: stalled, a grant on the bundle in force counted by h1 and h2 of three, scope this room, a user key, signed by it: the recovery concludes, and f4 is a founder
no trust root read: undecided, and it concludes nothing
stalled is read over the founders, whatever scope the widening states: live, counted `member`
the grant names a node key
the widening is signed by another key than the grant names
the grant's count is short: h1 alone of three
the grant names b0, and this node's bundle in force is b1 (h1..h4): h1 and h2 are two of four, the grant lapses
a grant by h1, h2 and h3 is three of four there, and the charter carries the duty: it resolves
the same where b1's charter drops the duty
G4: a grant by removed holders h1 and h2 naming b0, the reader at b2: no voices in force, refused
the reader's anchor names no first bundle
two tips: a grant on s1 by h1, h2 and h4, signers who hold only s1: three of s1's four
the same by h1 and h2 alone: two of four, short
charters differ, both carrying the duty: h1, h2 and h4 on s1 resolve
one founder seat and nothing else: a widening that also changes the protocol

the grant does not resolve for the reader: None
the scope in force decides: a later bundle dropping it
